business_process_change_analysis.process_shift_summary: The Specify Needs phase shifts from manually intensive stakeholder consultation, needs collation, option analysis, and business-case drafting toward AI-supported intake, synthesis, prioritization, and document generation. analysis.overall_gap_assessment: The largest gaps arise from the transition from manual, analyst-led needs identification to continuous, AI- and automation-enabled sensing. The current EC-02 profile contains a solid foundation in statistical analysis, contextual knowledge, trend identification, and communication, but weak representation of AI oversight, automation operations, unstructured data analysis, metadata traceability, and platform-based continuous intake. Future readiness depends less on advanced independent modeling and more on becoming an effective validator, interpreter, and governor of machine-assisted needs discovery.

process_shift_summary: The Analyse phase shifts from analyst-led, partly manual statistical examination and write-up preparation to automated, AI-enabled, modular analytical pipelines.
Output production, validation, commentary drafting, and standardized dissemination products become increasingly machine-assisted or machine-generated.
Human effort shifts upstream and downstream: configuring, supervising, interpreting, contextualizing, challenging, and explaining outputs rather than manually producing them.
Analysis becomes more continuous, iterative, real-time, and version-controlled, requiring stronger operational discipline and traceability.
Validation moves from periodic/manual review toward embedded, real-time anomaly detection and automated quality controls.
Analytical outputs must be reproducible, reusable, and seamlessly transferable into downstream dissemination processes.
implications_for_role: The role will spend less time on manual tabulation, routine commentary drafting, and basic trend identification performed directly by the analyst.
The role will spend more time reviewing AI-generated outputs for plausibility, bias, coherence, and policy or subject-matter relevance.
The role will increasingly be expected to interpret results in socio-economic context and tailor explanations for different user groups.
The role will need to work within modular analytical platforms, reusable workflows, and governed production pipelines rather than isolated analytical files.
The role will need to understand and document how outputs were generated, validated, versioned, and approved.
